note: Route tags and orders are our own classification of what each lead would show if it succeeds. A lead can sit on more than one route. Each route is ranked on its own: first the leads that most clearly fit it, then the rest by strength. The gauge shows the best score among its leads.

routes.label: Dishonesty
routes.desc: A document or declaration that misstated the facts to the court, the registry or the occupier.
routes.law: The test needs dishonesty in evidence, a statement or a concealed matter that was an operative cause of the decision (RBS v Highland [2013] EWCA Civ 328 [106], adopted in Takhar [2019] UKSC 13).

routes.label: Concealment
routes.desc: A record that existed but was withheld, removed or left out of the file.
routes.law: Limitation Act 1980 s.32 postpones time where a fact was deliberately concealed (Canada Square v Potter [2023] UKSC 41), but it does not itself reopen a judgment.

routes.label: Public bodies
routes.desc: A step taken by a registry, council, court office or other public body.
routes.law: Most of these lead to rectification, the Ombudsman or the Information Commissioner rather than to setting aside the 1987 judgment. Misfeasance in public office needs a knowing breach (Three Rivers [2003] 2 AC 1) and is not near being met.
